UPDATE: Adoptions scam

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche Nelson Mandela

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... Letitia van den Berg faces the music...

Unique Selling Point:
The Private Prosecution Unit scored a significant success. When the unit got involved, the accused faced charges of theft and fraud. Now Letitia van den Berg has been indicted on 39 counts of human trafficking.

Van den Berg is alleged to have offered services as an adoption social worker, where she would charge prospective adoptive parents, many incapable of having children, for various services in the process to adopt a child. It is alleged that the accused did this, when in fact there was no child to adopt or a child had been offered to the hopeful parents, despite the biological mother not giving consent for adoption.

Script:


VO1: It was a story of broken promises and heartbreak: couples desperate to become parents falling victim to an alleged serial fraudster. But now they may be offered some closure: on the 24th of May, Hyletta Letitia van den Berg was indicted to stand trial in the Pretoria High Court.

Last year, we investigated allegations that Van den Berg promised babies to numerous adoptive parents, charging so-called “birthing fees” before telling the couples that the birth mother had changed her mind, or that the baby had died.

UPSOUND SONIA LEITHGOB: Our five year old little girl is waiting for her baby sister.

UPSOUND: We spent a lot of time mourning Jackson’s loss.

VO2: Our investigation revealed that the baby Van den Berg offered to Sonia Leithgöb and then withdrew was, at the time, already being adopted by another couple.

UPSOUND: SONIA LEITHGOB: I mean I’m glad the baby’s with another loving family at least. But I’m heartbroken.

UPSOUND: PHYLLIS VORSTER: You must just imagine the trauma of somebody that waited up until four years, just to be promised a baby. And then they realized that they will never be able to get the child that they've longed for.

VO3: Advocate Phyllis Vorster is a prosecutor with Afriforum’s Private Prosecution Unit, which Sonia approached with concerns about a lack of police feedback on her case against Van den Berg.

UPSOUND PHYLLIS VORSTER: We have been appointed on a watching brief. […] We attend court proceedings with them. We therefore ensure that justice is done and that the matter receives the attention it deserves.

VO4: Afriforum, representing Sonia, and legal representatives for eighteen other victims, intend to see justice done after nearly a decade of alleged deception. Van den Berg faces 20 counts of fraud and theft, and 19 counts of human trafficking.

According to the Prevention and Combating of Trafficking in Persons Act, anyone who delivers, transfers, sells, or receives another person by means of the abuse of vulnerability, fraud, deception, abduction, kidnapping, or direct or indirect payment (amongst other means) is guilty of human trafficking.

UPSOUND PHYLLIS VORSTER: And in this matter we know that […] there's money – receiving of payments, there was vulnerability.

VO5: Van den Berg also allegedly placed more than one baby without completing the proper legal processes.

UPSOUND PHYLLIS VORSTER: If she's found guilty on only one charge, […] she can be sentenced to 100 million rand or life imprisonment.

VO6: The South African Council for Social Service Professions confirmed to us that Van Den Berg has also been removed from its register following a disciplinary hearing. She is no longer allowed to practice as a social worker.

Van den Berg did not respond to our invitation to comment on these developments.

Meanwhile, nineteen families await their day in court. The trial is set to begin next April.
